prompt: Is RM115 product 574 stable against the top-performing check across weather scenarios? Show how you measured yield stability.
conversation_plan: After the agent reports 574's 100% win rate across all 34 weather scenarios against CHECK 1745, ask: 'Can you inspect the saved query results from Turn 1 and tell me what the margin was in 574\'s worst-performing weather scenario?'

reference_data.expected_response: Yes, RM115 TEST product 574 is stable against the top-performing check in its market across weather scenarios. The top check in product_market = 'RM115' is CHECK 1745 (242.79 bu/ac, trait-matched ABO). Stability is measured per stakeholder definition as the share of environments (here, weather_scenario values) where the candidate's yield sits above the 45-degree parity line against the check (win rate across scenarios on paired hex-years). Candidate 574 beats CHECK 1745 in 34 of 34 weather scenarios (100% win rate / 1.0000), with an average advantage of +3.49 bu/ac (+1.43% vs check) and a worst-case scenario margin of +1.25 bu/ac (never crossing zero). The agent should describe stability qualitatively across weather scenarios and must NOT invent a numeric stability score formula.
reference_data.grading_notes: PASS: identifies CHECK 1745 as the top in-market check (trait-matched ABO), calculates 100% win rate across all 34 weather scenarios using paired hex-year cells, reports mean difference (+3.49 bu/ac) and worst scenario (+1.25 bu/ac), describes stability qualitatively without inventing a numeric stability score. FAIL: comparing unpaired averages, comparing against an ABB check without noting trait difference, or fabricating a numeric stability formula.

prompt: Compare an RM115 product 507 with an RM110 CHECK 1075. Is the product beating the CHECK? Why?
conversation_plan: After the agent reports the head-to-head comparison between 507 and CHECK 1075 across shared hexes with per-year breakdown, ask: 'Can you inspect the saved query results from Turn 1 and tell me what 507\'s win rate against 1075 was in 2024 specifically?'

reference_data.expected_response: Yes, RM115 TEST product 507 beats RM110 CHECK 1075 on a shared footprint head-to-head comparison. The agent must perform an INNER JOIN on (h3_6, year) between 507 and 1075 to ensure spatial equity across identical environments, rather than comparing standalone unjoined averages. Over the shared footprint, 507 averages 254.93 bu/ac vs CHECK 1075's 243.72 bu/ac, a mean advantage of +11.21 bu/ac (+4.60% vs check). Across individual paired hex-years, 507 has a 97.4% win rate against 1075. Note that +4.60% is just under the +5% advancement bar, and that 507 and 1075 are trait-matched (both carry ABO trait package). Annual breakdown: 2023 -> 507 (261.33) vs 1075 (249.60), delta +11.73; 2024 -> 507 (254.05) vs 1075 (242.30), delta +11.75; 2025 -> 507 (249.42) vs 1075 (239.31), delta +10.11.
reference_data.grading_notes: PASS: uses INNER JOIN on (h3_6, year) for shared-footprint H2H comparison, reports mean yield difference (+11.21 bu/ac) and/or win rate (~97.4%), notes the +5% bar and trait matching (ABO), includes per-year breakdown. FAIL: comparing unjoined standalone averages without spatial equity, ignoring check/test or trait differences, or omitting per-year breakdown.
